# API fixtures

Payloads captured verbatim from the running backend for the seeded synthetic well, so component
tests fail when the frontend drifts from the contract the API actually serves.

Captured with the API on `http://127.0.0.1:8099` after `seed_demo.py --reset`:

| File | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| `well-state.json` | `GET /api/v1/wells/{well_id}/state` |
| `well-npt.json` | `GET /api/v1/wells/{well_id}/npt` |
| `well-timeline.json` | `GET /api/v1/wells/{well_id}/timeline` |
| `well-twin.json` | `GET /api/v1/wells/{well_id}/twin` |
| `well-audit.json` | `GET /api/v1/wells/{well_id}/audit` |

The well is generated demo data (`SYNTH-DEMO-01 (synthetic data)`), so these files contain no
customer, well or field data. Every identifier inside them (`wel_…`, `opr_…`, `rec_…`) belongs to
that synthetic well and is regenerated by the seeder, which is why the tests read the ids from the
fixtures instead of hard-coding them.

These are contract anchors, not golden files: when the API changes shape on purpose, recapture them
from the real endpoint and commit the change in the same commit as the frontend fix that consumes it.
